source_row.stem: A facility uses ATP, or adenosine triphosphate, bioluminescence testing to verify cleaning effectiveness, and a housekeeping supervisor assumes this test is really meant to identify exactly which specific germ might be lurking on a surface. This method instead helps:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Objectively measure residual organic material on surfaces after cleaning, verifying cleaning adequacy, rather than identifying a specific pathogen as the supervisor is currently assuming","B":"Diagnose which specific pathogen may be present on a surface following an exposure or outbreak, similar to what the housekeeping supervisor is currently assuming this test does","C":"Offer little practical use for infection control despite its role in verifying cleaning adequacy, contrary to why this particular testing method is actually used","D":"Fully replace the need for any manual cleaning of surfaces between client uses, which is not the actual purpose of this particular testing method"}}
source_row.rationale: ATP bioluminescence testing objectively measures residual organic material on surfaces after cleaning, providing rapid, quantifiable verification of cleaning adequacy beyond visual inspection.
